Only 6 of 8 sections were provided for this note, so the last two sections are not described.

terms.meaning: the part of a PDF page that holds its drawing commands
the standard compression used inside PDF streams
a drawing command inside a PDF content stream
a small piece of data read in one step
a limit on size that stops the reading
a number that reveals whether data was damaged

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for PDF stream tests
sections.what: Brings in compression, the PDF object types, and the stream reader under test.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests build PDF streams by hand.

sections.name: metrics
sections.title: Test helper for page stream measurement
sections.what: Takes raw content pieces, optionally compresses them, and runs the page measurement with set budgets, returning the measured values.
sections.why: Likely reason: avoids repeating the same setup in every test.
sections.watch_out: Tests assume the measurement returns a pair of values, so a change in that shape breaks them.

sections.name: test_operator_boundaries_are_independent_of_chunk_size
sections.title: Drawing commands counted the same at any chunk size
sections.what: Reads the same content with several chunk sizes, compressed and raw, and checks the byte total and command count stay identical.
sections.why: Likely reason: the reader works in pieces, and where a piece ends must not change the result.
sections.watch_out: A change to chunk handling could split a command across pieces and change the count.

sections.name: test_empty_raw_and_flate_streams_and_exact_budget
sections.title: Empty streams and exact budgets
sections.what: Empty and short streams are measured correctly when the budget is exactly enough, and a total one byte over the budget raises an aggregate error.
sections.why: Likely reason: the budget must allow an exact fit and refuse any overflow.

sections.name: test_highly_compressed_multiple_output_chunks
sections.title: Highly compressed content read in pieces
sections.what: A half-megabyte run of repeated characters, compressed, is read in small chunks and gives the full byte count with one command.
sections.why: Likely reason: tiny compressed input can expand enormously, so reading must be done in pieces.

sections.name: test_flate_integrity_not_successful_truncation
sections.title: Damaged compressed content fails
sections.what: A compressed stream that is truncated, has trailing extra data, or has a wrong checksum raises a value or zlib error instead of returning partial counts.
sections.why: Likely reason: partial counts would look like a successful reading.

sections.name: test_unrecognized_content_filter_predictor_and_cancellation
sections.title: Rejects unsupported PDF content and honors cancel
sections.what: Checks that the PDF page reader stops with a clear error when a page uses an image format it cannot handle (DCTDecode, a JPEG filter) or a compression setting called a predictor. It also checks that a cancel request raises an error and stops the work.
sections.why: Likely reason: unsupported PDF content should be rejected loudly rather than read wrongly, and cancellation must work so the app does not keep running on unwanted jobs.
sections.watch_out: The test matches error text containing the words filter and predictor, so rewording those error messages will break it.

sections.name: test_vector_budget_is_actual
sections.title: Caps the number of drawing commands
sections.what: Checks that the reader counts PDF drawing commands such as m, S and re (line and rectangle operations) and stops with a vector operators error once the count passes the allowed limit of 2.
sections.why: Likely reason: a cap on drawing commands stops a very detailed drawing from using unlimited time or memory. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The limit counts real drawing commands, so changing how commands are counted changes when this error appears.

summary: Tests the reader that counts drawing commands in a PDF page's content streams, including compressed and damaged streams.
purpose: Confirms the page measurement is accurate regardless of how the data is split or compressed, and that damaged or oversized streams are refused.
why: Likely reason: PDF page content can be split into pieces and compressed, so reading must be consistent. Reason not stated in the code beyond this.
how: Builds content streams by hand, optionally compresses them, runs the page measurement with byte and vector budgets, and compares the returned counts or expected errors.
inputs: Raw content bytes, compression choice, chunk size settings, and budget values chosen in each test.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest.
risks: Only six of the eight sections needing notes were provided, so two parts of this file are not described here.
debug: Check the failing test name, its chunk size and budget values, and whether the measurement helper returned the expected pair of values.
